Maya (CS): quick thread — I'm assembling the customer follow-up for BrightApps. Incident this morning affected embeddings lookups; they saw increased latency and ~2% failed requests. Drafting timeline + customer-facing blurb here. need engineering + SRE sign-off before i send.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT INC-2026-57 resolved — severity: sev2. Page routed to oncall at 09:12 UTC, mitigated by 09:47 UTC.

Raj (Oncall): short recap from my side: after a rolling kernel upgrade in the dedicated cluster we started seeing memory pressure around 09:10. Our eviction heuristic kicked in, which caused the KV cache to drop entries. That triggered a fallback to CPU-path for embeddings which increased latency and led to some request timeouts.

Jenna (SRE): timeline (short):
```
09:08 - autoscaling event triggered, nodes rebalanced
09:10 - memory pressure spike detected on node ded-34
09:11 - eviction heuristic evicting cache shards
09:12 - BrightApps alerts + paging to Raj
09:20 - increased 95th p99 latency observed, error rate up ~2%
09:27 - temporary circuit breaker engaged for heavy batch workloads
09:35 - manual cache warm-up and restart of affected pods
09:47 - system stabilized, latency within SLOs, error rate normalized
```

Tom (Support): BrightApps reported impact in their staging and a few live requests timed out. They did not lose data but saw degraded UX for search/autocomplete. They asked for: timeline, root cause, what we did, and what we will do to avoid recurrence. Also asked whether credits will be provided.

Maya (CS): Draft customer email (first pass) — please review tone and technical details:

```
Subject: Update on this morning's embeddings degradation (09:10 UTC)

Hi Team,

We're reaching out about the issue your team experienced around 09:10 UTC today that affected embeddings lookups. Summary:

- What happened: A memory pressure event in a dedicated inference node caused our KV cache to be evicted. As a result, some requests fell back to a slower CPU path leading to higher latency and a small percent of request timeouts.
- Impact: Some of your real-time embeddings/lookups experienced delays (up to ~6x) and roughly 2% of requests timed out between 09:12 and 09:47 UTC.
- What we did: Our on-call team identified the eviction cascade, restarted affected pods, and performed a cache warm-up which restored normal performance.

Actions we're taking to prevent this:
- Tweak eviction thresholds and add a rolling-memory-safety gate (ETA: 1 week).
- Add proactive alerting for shard-level cache evictions (ETA: 3 days).
- Run a canary of the kernel upgrade across a test slice before cluster-wide rollouts (ETA: next deployment window).

We apologize for the disruption. We can offer a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of this month\u2019s bill for the affected service as a gesture — let us know if that works.

Thanks,
Maya on behalf of Redwood Inference Support
```

Alice (Eng): wording looks good. Small technical nit: the root cause is an interaction between our eviction heuristic and the kernel reclaim behavior after the node rebalance; suggest changing "memory pressure event" -> "reclaim behavior during node rebalance". Also propose adding one more preventative action: reserve a small pinned memory pool for KV shards so they are resilient to short reclaim bursts (prototype in progress).

Raj (Oncall): agree with Alice. For the ETA list: the cache eviction alert (3 days) is realistic, the safety gate (1 week) maybe 10 days if we include test windows. I'll own the implementation of monitoring and can do the alerting PR today.

Maya (CS): updated draft blurb to be slightly less technical and added the credit offer. Also added a one-paragraph non-technical summary for execs. Putting final draft here: please react with :thumbsup: if ready to send, or reply with edits.

```
Customer-facing summary (short):
We experienced a temporary degradation in embeddings lookups due to internal cache evictions during a routine node rebalance. Performance returned to normal within ~35 minutes. We have implemented immediate mitigations and are scheduling follow-up safeguards to reduce the chance of recurrence.
```

StatusPageBot: Suggested public status update (short):
```
Title: Degraded embeddings performance — resolved
Impact: Users may have experienced higher latency and intermittent errors for embeddings lookups.
Status: Resolved
Incident window: 09:10 - 09:47 UTC
What we're doing: Implementing additional alerts and eviction safeguards; kernel upgrade rollouts will have a canary phase.
```

Tom (Support): From CS side i recommend offering the 5% credit and a follow-up call with their platform engineer if they want deeper technical walk-through. BrightApps is enterprise; they value post-incident transparency.

Jenna (SRE): Action items (who -> what):
- Raj: open alerting PR for shard eviction (today)
- Alice: design pinned-memory prototype and doc schedule (this week)
- Jenna: add canary step to kernel rollout playbook (next deploy)
- Maya/Tom: send customer email and schedule optional call (today)

Raj (Oncall): i'll post the alerting PR link here once created.

Maya (CS): thanks all — i'll wait for the :thumbsup: and then send to BrightApps with cc to their TAM. please add any edits inline. planning to send by 11:30 UTC. :wave:

Alice (Eng): :thumbsup: from eng

Jenna (SRE): :thumbsup:

Tom (Support): :thumbsup:

Maya (CS): sending now. will copy thread with timestamp and attach incident timeline in the support ticket.
